ch00.card: Start here. What you are about to see.
ch00.s01.c1: So what is this? A research project. It is building a language model, a program that reads text and writes an answer.
ch00.s01.c2: Two goals. Skills and careful thinking first, then learning from only a few examples.
ch00.s01.c3: It is not an app. GitHub lists 0 releases. Nothing here is finished.
ch00.s02.c1: Goal one: skills and careful thinking. Did it work?
ch00.s02.c2: At the smallest size, 3 million learned numbers, an earlier design scored higher than an ordinary same-size model. Six separate training runs, each from its own random start. It won all six.
ch00.s02.c3: Goal two, learning from only a few examples, is only partly shown so far. Brand-new kinds of rule are mostly missed.
ch00.s06.c1: Now the machine, in four parts. First, a reader. It gives each letter a meaning from the whole question. Its main part is borrowed and frozen. Our practice never changes it.
ch00.s06.c2: A thinker thinks in rounds, which are laps of looking and thinking. Its settings start from scratch, set only by our practice.
ch00.s06.c3: A stop switch says done. It is built, but never run.
ch00.s06.c4: The talker writes one line a turn. Today it is a small stand-in.
ch00.s06.c5: Outside, a calculator. The talker's line calls it. The reader reads it.
ch00.s08.c1: Here is the trick to remembering them. Picture a student doing a word problem.
ch00.s08.c2: A translator reads the question. Then a team of note-takers thinks it over, round after round.
ch00.s08.c3: The final-answer writer may write a request slip. A pocket calculator, outside the team, sends back a slip. The translator reads it.
ch00.s08.c4: A little bell rings when they are done, and one person writes the final answer. Each colour always means the same part. This is an analogy, not a diagram of the code.
ch00.s09.c1: How sure are we? Think of a traffic light. Green means tested, and a result file exists. For example, with the calculator outside, scores matched the earlier design in 6 runs, at the smallest size.
ch00.s09.c2: Amber means built, but never tested. No real training run was ever done. Which tag fits the stop switch? Amber.
ch00.s09.c3: Grey means placeholder. It does not exist yet. The English talker is planned, not built.
ch00.s11.c1: A vector is a list of numbers, like a note card. The reader turns each letter into one. How long is a card? Part 1 tells you. Picture only means a drawing, not a measurement.
ch00.s11.c2: A round is one lap of looking at the whole question, passing notes, and thinking. The thinker does lap after lap.
ch00.s12.c1: A call is the talker's line, a text request to the outside calculator. Sub 12, 5 means take 5 away from 12.
ch00.s12.c2: The reply, also text: 7. The whole reader reads it. Made-up example: sub 12, 5 = 7.
ch00.s12.c3: New design, being built: the talker writes the calls. Any other line is the final answer.
ch00.s13.c1: Practice is homework. The model tries a question, is told the right answer, and every setting is nudged a tiny bit. One nudge is one update.
ch00.s13.c2: Now the exam. Questions kept aside are never used in practice. The model has never seen them, so the score is fair.
ch00.s14.c1: A score is points out of 100, the share of questions answered right. Here, 73.01 points on 6,040 questions kept aside. Is that good?
ch00.s14.c2: A copy is one separate run from its own random start. Six copies are six chances to see the same result.
ch00.s14.c3: Careful: 73.01 is one copy, at the smallest size, on an earlier design.
ch00.s15.c1: To judge 73.01, we need a yardstick: a plain model. Same size, same practice, same borrowed reader, but ordinary.
ch00.s15.c2: Guess first. On the same 6,040 questions kept aside, the plain model scored 67.12 points out of 100, and ours scored 73.01.
ch00.s15.c3: Careful: these two scores come from one copy, at the smallest size, on an earlier design. We do not claim it holds at bigger sizes.
ch00.s19.c1: Three promises. One: every real number comes from a project file, like the plain model's score, traced to its file.
ch00.s19.c2: Two: pictures that only illustrate carry a tag, like picture only or made-up example. They are never real measurements.
ch00.s19.c3: Three: what is not proven stays amber or grey. Nothing is released. Next, one made-up apple question, followed from start to finish.
